spots.name: Ghazanchetsots Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Holy Savior Cathedral, commonly referred to as Ghazanchetsots, is an Armenian Apostolic cathedral in Shusha in Azerbaijan. It is the cathedra of the Diocese of Artsakh of the Armenian Apostolic Church. Standing 35 metres (115 ft) high, Ghazanchetsots is one of the largest Armenian churches in the world.

spots.name: We Are Our Mountains
spots.summary: We Are Our Mountains is a monument north of Stepanakert in the region of Nagorno-Karabakh, Azerbaijan. The sculpture, completed in 1967 by Sargis Baghdasaryan, is widely regarded as a symbol of the Armenian heritage of Nagorno-Karabakh, with some considering it to be a symbol of Armenian identity as a whole.

spots.name: Shusha fortress
spots.summary: The Shusha fortress or Shushi fortress is a fortress surrounding the historical centre of Shusha. The newly conquered castle town was called "Panahabad fortress" named after Panah Ali Khan who together with Melik Shahnazar was the founder of the fort. In later years, the city was just called "Fortress".

spots.name: Kanach Zham

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint John the Baptist Church, commonly known as Kanach Zham, was an Armenian Apostolic church in Shusha in Azerbaijan, in the region of Nagorno-Karabakh, located just uphill from the Ghazanchetsots Cathedral. Kanach Zham means "Green Chapel" in Armenian, which refers to the previously green domes of the church.

spots.name: Yukhari Govhar Agha Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Yukhari Govhar Agha Mosque, also called the Great Mosque of Govhar Agha, is a Shia Islam mosque located in the city of Shusha, Azerbaijan.

spots.name: Ashaghi Govhar Agha Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ashaghi Govhar Agha Mosque is a mosque in Shusha, Azerbaijan.

photo.author: Press Service of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan

spots.name: Victory Square
spots.summary: Renaissance Square, commonly known as Veratsnound or Revival Square or Victory Square was the main square in the city of Stepanakert, Nagorno-Karabakh, Azerbaijan. It was developed in 1994 following the Battle of Shusha and the securing of the area by the Artsakh Defense Army.

photo.author: Press Service of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan

spots.name: Vagif Mausoleum
spots.summary: Vagif Mausoleum is a mausoleum located in Shusha, Azerbaijan. It is built to honor Molla Panah Vagif, a poet, diplomat and vizier

spots.name: House of Natavan
spots.summary: The House of Khurshidbanu Natavan, also known as the Palace of Natavan, Daughter of the Khan, is an 18th or 19th-century historical and architectural monument, and a museum in Shusha, Azerbaijan.

spots.name: Shushi Carpet Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Shushi Carpet Museum was a museum in Shusha that operated while the city was under the control of the Republic of Artsakh. It was founded by Vardan Astsatryan in 2011 and opened to the public in 2013.

spots.name: Ganja Gate
spots.summary: Ganja Gate is one of the three main gates of the Shusha fortress in Shusha, Azerbaijan, and is located on the fortress's northern side. The other two gates are the Iravan Gate and the Aghoghlan Gate.

spots.name: House-Museum of Bulbul

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The House-Museum of Bulbul was the Shusha branch of the Bulbul memorial museum in Baku, Azerbaijan, until 1992. It was previously in a ruined status but has been recently restored.

spots.name: Saatli Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Saatli Mosque is a mosque located in Shusha, Azerbaijan.

spots.name: Mamayi Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mamayi Mosque is a Shia Islam mosque, located in Shusha, Azerbaijan, approximately 350 kilometres (220 mi) from Baku, the Azerbaijani capital.

spots.name: Shusha Museum of History

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Shusha Museum of History was one of 8 museums located in Shusha, Azerbaijan. It was built in 1969 and contained up to 5,000 exhibits. The museum was closed after the capture of Shusha on May 8, 1992.

spots.name: Mardinli Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mardinli Mosque is a former Shia Muslim mosque, now in ruins, located in Shusha, in the Karabakh region in Azerbaijan.

spots.name: "Khan gizi" spring
spots.summary: "Khan gizi" spring is a spring located next to Khan's daughter Natevan's palace in the Çöl Qala neighborhood of Shusha. The spring was built in the 19th century by the order of Khurshidbanu Natavan.

spots.name: Statue of Uzeyir Hajibeyov
spots.summary: Statue of Uzeyir Hajibeyov is a monument erected in 1985 to Uzeyir Hajibeyov, an Azerbaijani composer, musicologist-scientist, publicist, dramatist, pedagogue and public figure, founder of modern Azerbaijani professional music art and national opera, composer of the national anthem of the Republic of Azerbaijan, author of the first opera in the Muslim East, in his hometown of Shusha.

spots.name: Khoja Marjanli Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Khoja Marjanli Mosque was a former Shia Islam mosque, now in ruins, located in Shusha, in the Karabakh region. It is located on the Mirza Alakbar Sabir street of the Khoja Marjanli neighborhood of Shusha.

spots.name: House of Sadigjan

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: House of Sadigjan is a residential building built in the 19th century in Shusha, Merdinli neighborhood. The house where Mirza Asad oghlu Sadig, an Azerbaijani musician, tarzan, composer and developer of the Azerbaijani tar, lived. The building is registered in the name of Sadigov Rahim, the grandson of tarzen Sadigjan.

photo.author: Press Service of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan

spots.name: Divankhana Square
spots.summary: Divankhana Square or Bazaar-bashi is the first and the largest city square located at the entrance to Shusha, Azerbaijan from the side of the Ganja Gate. The largest shopping street Rasta Bazaar starts from this area.

spots.name: Ibrahim Khalil Khan palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ibrahim Khalil Khan palace or Ibrahim Khalil Khan castle is a historical palace located in the south-eastern part of Shusha, near Dashalty village. In some sources, the palace is also called palace of Karabakh Khans.

spots.name: Asad-bey's House
spots.summary: Asad-bey's House is a historical and architectural monument of the early 18th century being located in Shusha. The house belonged to one of the famous representatives of the noble family of Shusha - to Asad-bey.

spots.name: Bust of Molla Panah Vagif
spots.summary: Bust of Molla Panah Vagif is a bust raised in the honour of the famous Azerbaijani poet, political and public figure of the 18th century, Molla Panah Vagif. It was destroyed after the capture of the city of Shusha in 1992 by the Armenian forces.

spots.name: Haji Gulular Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Haji Gulular Palace is a historical and architectural monument located in the city of Shusha. The palace was built in 1849 in the Chukhur mehelle by the order of the merchant of the second guild Gulu Mahammadali oghlu.

spots.name: Two-Storeyed Caravanserai
spots.summary: Two-Storeyed Caravanserai is a caravanserai built in Shusha in the 19th century. It is a two-storeyed hotel-style caravanserai in the Sheytan Bazaar part of Shusha.

photo.author: Press Service of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan

spots.name: Memorial Complex of Participants of the Great Patriotic War
spots.summary: Memorial complex of the participants of the Great Patriotic War is a monument located on Khalil Mammadov Street in the city of Shusha, Azerbaijan. It is dedicated to the participants of the Second World War.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Memorial Complex of Participants of the Great Patriotic War (Shusha)

spots.name: Khankendi Stadium
spots.summary: Stepanakert Republican Stadium or Khankendi Stadium is a stadium in Stepanakert, Nagorno-Karabakh, Azerbaijan.

photo.author: Press Service of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan

spots.name: Shirin Su bathhouse
spots.summary: Shirin Su bathhouse or the Bathhouse of the Fresh Water is a historical monument located in the city of Shusha, Azerbaijan. It was built in 1878–1880 at the order of Khurshidbanu Natavan by the architect of Kerbelayi Sefikhan Garabaghy.

photo.author: Press Service of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan

spots.name: Khanlig Mukhtar caravanserai
spots.summary: Khanlig Mukhtar caravanserai is a nationally important caravanserai belonging to the Shusha State Historical-Architectural Reserve, located at 29 M.F. Akhundov Street, Shusha.

spots.name: Khoja Marjanly's Spring
spots.summary: Khoja Marjanly's Spring is a historical spring located in the city of Shusha, Nagorno-Karabakh, in the Khoja Marjanly neighbourhood, near the mosque with the same name. It was built in the 18th century.

spots.name: Bust of Bulbul
spots.summary: Bust of Bulbul is a bronze bust erected in the city of Shusha.
